units.La refonte de tousimparfaits.com que vou: The tousimparfaits.com rebuild you just walked through, the sixty logo routes next door, the nine-language translation: it’s free. No license, no invoice, nothing expected back. Keep it, trash it, slice it into a Shopify theme — it’s yours.
units.Ce qui suit explique qui je suis, pourqu: What follows explains who I am, why I did it, and what I can do next if you feel like going further. The pricing part is short and blunt.
units.Refonte offerte ≈ 500 $ d'usage réel 4 à: Free rebuild ≈ $500 in real usage 4 to 5 hours of my time, one Sunday Nothing expected in return Open source, MIT license

units.J'ai fait mes armes en ingénierie social: I cut my teeth in social engineering — the human factor, the one that breaks before the firewalls do — working for the intelligence services. It’s a job that teaches you two things: how people actually decide, and how an entire system rests on three people and two passwords.
units.Aujourd'hui je suis entrepreneur Interne: Today I’m an internet entrepreneur, based between New York and Lisbon, and a consultant on two subjects: cybersecurity and applied AI. I build my own products — an eSIM carrier, a news app — and I work on other people’s when the subject appeals to me.
units.Concrètement, ce que je sais faire de me: Concretely, what I can build with my own hands: sites and apps that convert, AI agents that do the work instead of talking about it, databases and team workflows that hold up under load, audits that find what will break before it breaks.
units.Et surtout, il y a le hors-champ. Avec m: And above all, there’s what you don’t see. With my teams at megastack.sh and calliope.agency, we eventually built our own models for branding, web design and web app development. Not recycled prompts: models trained and tooled for the job, and frighteningly good at it. They already run on my own companies — Openline, cupof.news — and on our clients’ projects.
units.C'est exactement ce que vous avez sous l: That’s exactly what you’re looking at: about five hundred dollars of real usage and four to five hours of my time — one Sunday, multitasking with my other projects, while a dozen hours of agents ran in the background — and this is the level of quality it produces. And that’s only design and front end — I haven’t even started on the rest: heavy development, infrastructure, automation and workflows.
units.Alors je me suis dit : tiens, je vais pr: So I thought: let me offer Tev and the team a hand.
units.Au printemps 2020, en l'espace de trois: In spring 2020, in the space of three months, I lost my professional mentor, my biological father and my girlfriend at the time — and the world stopped on top of it all. I resigned from the system. Not metaphorically: I quit, and I stayed on the internet.
units.C'est là que je suis tombé sur Tev (entr: That’s when I came across Tev (among plenty of other things, and reconnecting with childhood friends and video games). And then, above all, what got built around him: the successive teams, the people arriving, the people leaving, the formats finding their shape, the company growing without ever losing its tone. All the way to today’s full octopus — Odyssée included, the esport, the food, the merch, all of it.
units.Je ne dis pas ça pour faire joli avant d: I’m not saying this to look good before I talk money. I’m saying it because it’s the only reason this rebuild exists: nobody asked for it, nobody is paying for it. I watched the video where you say you have to start Tous Imparfaits over, that the branding isn’t keeping up, that no logo works across the whole range. And I did what I know how to do, on a Sunday, instead of leaving a comment.
units.C'est aussi mon test d'entrée. Vous juge: It’s also my way in. You judge the work before you talk to me — no portfolio, no discovery call, no deck. The thing is live, you click, you see.

But people discover, follow and share a brand long before they can order from it. You’ll see over time whether there’s reason to open up — and the day you do, the interface won’t have any catching up to do.

units.Aucun jugement sur le site actuel : il t: No judgment on the current site: it works, it sells, it has a personality, and there’s real work behind it — this isn’t a rebuild as a verdict. I simply think my setup of AI design agents turns out good things: a very deliberate style and genuinely useful features that add value to a web presence without breaking anything that already works — up to you to decide whether it speaks to you.
units.Autant être net tout de suite : ce que v: Let’s be clear right away: what you’re looking at is a static showcase, made to show the potential of the journey in an afternoon’s work — not a production site. Nothing is connected to real stock, real payments or real orders.

units.La suite est un escalier de quatre march: What comes next is a four-step staircase, detailed in the block below: cut it into a Shopify theme, then build around Shopify, then leave it — Stripe payments direct, a secure NoSQL database, a clean API and an MCP server to plug stock and content into Notion, Airtable, ClickUp or your own agents. And beyond that, infrastructure of your own: self-hosted n8n, Ollama, models and workflows. Step 3 strongly recommended
units.Pour information, et pas pour facturatio: For information, not for invoicing. Here’s what this rebuild cost: 26,607 credits and 10 hrs 15 of machine time. With my private “frontier AI” model provider, a thousand credits go for $17 to $22 depending on task complexity — how many models are called, how deep the reasoning goes, how many round trips — which puts the whole thing at around $500.
units.À côté de ça, quatre à cinq heures de mo: On top of that, four to five hours of my time, one Sunday, multitasking with my other projects. That’s the usual ratio, and that’s the whole point: my hours steer, its hours produce.
units.Notez les trois zéros du relevé : 0,00 e: Note the three zeros in the report: 0.00 in image, video and audio. Nothing was generated. Every photograph on these pages is yours, taken from your site — a rebuild is judged on the brand’s real visuals, not on flattering renders that will never exist for real.

MIT license: clone it, cut it up, resell it, no permission needed. No dependencies, no build step — a static server and it’s live.

units.[04] 技 Ce que je peux faire ensuite: [04] 技 What I can do next
units.De la découpe Shopifyà la pieuvre entièr:
From a Shopify cut-up
to the whole octopus.
units.Par ordre croissant d'engagement. Vous p: In increasing order of commitment. Pick what’s useful to you, in whatever order you like.
units.ADécoupe et intégration ShopifyLe templa: AShopify cut-up and integrationThe template turned into a clean Shopify theme: editable sections, reusable blocks, native cart and checkout, metafields for collections and gift tiers. Delivered ready to publish, not ready to debug.
units.BEntourer Shopify, sans encore le quitte: BBuild around Shopify, without leaving it yetThe middle step, and the least risky: we keep Shopify for payments and compliance and take back everything else — the storefront becomes static and fast, the catalog and the content move out of the admin, and the missing views (categories, filterable listings, search, customer account) get built in the design system already in place.
units.CSortir de Shopify — et c'est ce que je:
CLeave Shopify — and this is what I recommendWhen the subscription, the commission and the theme’s limits become the real cost, you replace the black box: Stripe direct for payments (with Apple Pay, Google Pay, PayPal, SEPA and taxes handled), a secure NoSQL database for the catalog, the stock, the orders and the customers, a clean API in front, and an MCP server on top. MCP is the real turning point: it plugs the catalog and the stock into what you already use — Notion, Airtable, ClickUp, a spreadsheet, or agents directly — so the team manages content and stock from its own tools, without ever touching code. You get back the margin, the speed, and ownership of your data.What the API + MCP pair really unlocks. Once the catalog, the stock and the orders sit behind a clean API and an MCP server, any tool that speaks MCP plugs straight in — and today, they all speak MCP. Your accounting, your CRM, a chatbot on the site, an agent chasing abandoned carts: those stop being integrations to develop one by one and become a connection.

The clearest example: a WhatsApp number that answers for the whole store. “How many sales today?” “Revenue this month, against last month?” “How many Yokai hoodies left in M?” “Put the Mystery Pack at − 20 % until Sunday.” You ask, it answers; you decide, it executes. From an airport queue, without opening a laptop and without training anyone on a back office. With a scope per person: who can read what, who can decide what.

The same socket works for the software nobody ever wants to open — CRM, accounting, ERP, tracking spreadsheets. Instead of learning their interface, you talk to them. And it works just as well for customer service: “where is my order?”, “I picked the wrong size”, “do you ship to Japan?” — the order gets read, an exchange gets offered, the return label goes out, and a human only steps back in when it’s genuinely needed. You answer at night without staying up. And it isn’t magic, it just became accessible: the real ceiling is the token cost, the hours I have available and the budget you put in. We size it in that order.
units.DUne infra maison, chez vousLa marche d': DInfrastructure of your own, in-houseThe step after that, for anyone who wants to stop renting: self-hosted n8n for automation (orders, emails, stock, alerts, publishing), Ollama and self-hosted models for writing, translation, support triage and moderation — on your machines, with no per-token bill and without sending your data to a third party. Plus the rest of the toolkit: servers, a network closed by default, backups, dashboards, monitoring.
units.ECalendrier social tenu par une personne: EA social calendar run by a person, powered by agentsI don’t sell autopilot. I tested full auto on my own brands, Openline included, and for restaurant and hotel clients through digital.spot — a business currently on hold, but the lessons are in: it produces lukewarm volume and damages a brand faster than silence does. The setup I recommend is the opposite: your editorial calendar in ClickUp, Notion or Google Docs — one post, one date, one language, one status — and an in-house agent that syncs it all, prepares the variants per network and per language, and drops two or three generated bonuses (a short video, a visual, a first draft of a caption) straight into the card. Approval stays 100 % human, inside the tool, in one click. Full transparency: I’ve never run mass B2C myself, for lack of time — but it really isn’t complicated, I watch it run at Openline, and in a month or two it will run better still.
units.FRebranding et redesign de tout l'écosys:
FRebranding and redesign across the whole ecosystemThe six categories announced in “On doit recommencer Tous Imparfaits”, laid out under a single visual system that can actually hold. Then every site in the ecosystem brought into that system — same grid, same typography, same conversion logic.The octopus, concretely. Tokyo Cards sells Japanese TCG — Pokémon, One Piece, Dragon Ball, mystery boosters — to an international audience: there, the subject is the product page, availability and languages, not fashion. The Musée Odyssée sells nothing yet: it makes people dream, it announces, it gathers a community around a place that doesn’t exist. Onamaesama carries drawn patterns, AMONE, Kanji Burger and the SAIBĀ café talk food and physical venues, the esport talks schedule, roster and results, and Tous Imparfaits talks drops and cuts. As many different sales languages as there are different design problems.

So what has to be shared isn’t the look — a museum that looked like a t-shirt shop would fail on both counts. It’s the foundation: a shared grid and type scale, a set of components (product page, gift tier, proof block, form) you adapt instead of rewriting, one way of writing prices, stock and lead times, one language system, and color tokens where each entity sets its own hue without breaking the others. You build it once; after that each entity costs days, not months.

And the most underrated benefit arrives when the whole ecosystem shares the same API and the same MCP server: it runs from a single place. Tokyo Cards stock, Tous Imparfaits orders, the esport numbers — and Odyssée bookings the day they exist — in the same conversation.
units.GIci Japon Village, enfin chez vousHuit:
GIci Japon Village, finally your ownEight houses, twenty-two rooms in Takasago — and not one address that belongs to you: bookings go through Keikaku and the rest of the traffic gets captured by the aggregators. I’m offering you a site of your own for the Village, built to be found (French, English and Japanese SEO, room pages, reviews, routes from Narita and Haneda), with an in-house booking engine synced with your provider rather than against it: same calendar, same availability, two channels. And the Village plugged into the rest of the octopus: the same visual system, a stay that can arrive with a Tous Imparfaits tee or a Tokyo Cards card, and operations — check-ins, cleaning, guest messages — in the same workflows as the rest of the group.

And above all: take back control of the price. Dynamic pricing wired only to your own channels — the Village site and the social accounts around it — so that direct is always the best deal: payment by Stripe, PayPal, bank transfer, even crypto if you want it. Zero commission to a third party, nobody between your audience and your houses. That’s exactly where influence converts: someone who has followed you for ten years books with you, on your page, at your price, in three clicks.

And I haven’t forgotten what the Village stands for: not just an asset in Japan, but the project you and Akiko imagined together, and the daily life of the people who keep it running — Nuri welcoming guests to the houses since the very beginning. A direct channel that works is also what keeps that team going, properly and for the long haul.
units.HEt le resteAudit de sécurité et de conf: HAnd the restSecurity and compliance audit (the missing legal pages, among other things), performance and SEO, email funnels, internal tooling, dashboards, whatever you haven’t had time to name yet.
units.[05] 貨 Comment je me rémunère: [05] 貨 How I get paid
units.Aucune n'est un forfait imposé. On mélan: None of them is a package imposed on you. We mix them depending on what you want to get, what I think I can genuinely change, and the level of involvement we choose together.
units.Je facture l’usage constaté de mes modèl: I bill the measured usage of my models, multiplied by a coefficient of 1 to 5 depending on the complexity of the work involved and the level of fine-tuning required.
units.Une demande simple, administrative ou po: A simple, administrative or one-off request
units.Une landing page, une page de vente, un: A landing page, a sales page, a theme
units.Une chaîne d’agents multilingue qui tour: A multilingual agent chain running in production
units.Un système nettement plus poussé — infra: A far more ambitious system — in-house infrastructure, a platform, anything that has to last
units.Le plancher, pas le plafond, de ma rémun: The floor of what I earn, not the ceiling
units.À l'heure ou à la journée: By the hour or by the day
units.Mon temps de cerveau et de mains, séparé: My brain and my hands, billed separately from the machine. Invoiced from the European Union or from the United States, whichever suits your accounting — intra-EU VAT or a non-EU invoice.
units.Pour une implication qui dépasse la pres: For involvement that goes beyond a service contract. A monthly retainer at three times the French gross minimum wage — about €5,600 a month based on the SMIC in force on June 1st, 2026 (€1,867.02 gross) — plus equity or a profit share in the projects where I have measurable impact.
units.Concrètement, voilà à quoi ça ressemble: Here is what that looks like in practice: I work with no deadline, calmly, very part-time — but regularly, and on every detail and every project you want. No sprints, no tight back-planning, no invoice creeping up: a continuous flow that moves every week. That’s what makes the price / quality / turnaround ratio so good — my models absorb the volume, and all I have to arbitrate is taste and priorities.
units.Que ce soit clair : sans deadline et à t: To be clear: no deadline and part-time does not mean low impact. It’s the opposite. The time I don’t spend keeping a schedule, I spend on substance — and on every entity I can touch: the store, the brand, the channels, the esport, the internal tools, the things that don’t exist yet. Improving what runs, rebuilding what no longer holds, innovating where nobody has had the time to look. And with no limit on subject: web, design, infrastructure, data, AI, automation, security — if there’s technology behind it, I can handle it, and a year of that regime changes a company far more than a quarter of sprints.
units.Et sur ce mode-là, on la joue réglo sur: And on that arrangement, we play it straight on the rest. Tokens go back to 1× — the measured cost, reimbursed to the cent, with no complexity coefficient: the retainer already covers that. With a floor and a budget set together, so nobody discovers the figure at the end of the month. And my rates don’t move either: still €50 an hour or €500 a day, and only if the free time I give you for that triple minimum wage genuinely calls for an exceptional bonus. Honestly, that should stay rare.
units.C’est un fonctionnement de CDI, mais fac: It works like a permanent job, but billable from abroad: you get the consistency and the availability of a part-time employee without the contract, and I keep control of my own schedule. On those terms, and with models reimbursed at 1×, I genuinely believe I can have a substantial impact across every entity of the octopus rather than on one site at a time.
units.Le fixe couvre la disponibilité et la ré: The retainer covers availability and consistency, not hours
units.Aucune deadline imposée de part et d'aut: No deadline imposed on either side — it moves continuously, not in bursts
units.Le périmètre est ouvert : le site, la ma: The scope is open: the site, the brand, the automation, the infrastructure, the details that have been dragging for two years
units.Je le fais sur mon temps libre, en alter: I do it in my free time, alternating with my own companies
units.L'impact vise le fond, pas le délai : re: The impact aims at substance, not speed: rebuilds, continuous improvement, innovation, whatever the technology involved
units.L'intéressement se discute projet par pr: The profit share is discussed project by project, not as a block
units.Des sponsorings, gratuits pour moi et me: Sponsorships, free for me and my boys
units.Vous me payez en visibilité : des sponso: You pay me in visibility: free sponsorships on your content for my B2C companies and those of my boys. Nothing leaves your cash flow, and on my side an acquisition channel worth far more than an invoice.
units.Openline — eSIM dans plus de 210 pays, b: Openline — eSIM in more than 210 countries, automatic switching between several Tier 1 networks (openline.com)
units.cupof.news — app de news : dix histoires: cupof.news — news app: ten stories every morning, 9 languages, freemium with a low-cost personalized option, launching in October (cupof.news)
units.Personne ne choisit une option et s’y en: Nobody picks one option and gets locked into it. Depending on the project, the month or the year, the mix shifts: a little direct cash here, a profit share there, sponsorships when the timing is right, and model reimbursement running in the background. We can revisit it whenever you like, with nothing to renegotiate.
units.NB 1 — Openline face à Ubigi, autant le: NB 1 — Openline against Ubigi, let’s get it out of the way. I know exactly who already sponsors you. My argument is simple: we’re cheaper, and we switch between several MVNOs and carriers per country, where Ubigi is the consumer brand of a single virtual operator — Transatel, part of the NTT group (Transatel). On paper and in the field, it shows. If exclusivity isn’t a problem for them, let’s go; if it is, we talk about cupof.news and make nothing of it.
units.NB 2 — la discrétion fait partie du deal: NB 2 — discretion is part of the deal. If you feel like working with me and talking about it, one thing first: I’m not looking to become an influencer, and I don’t want to be on camera. I work for governments, large groups and politically exposed people — in this job, personal visibility is a risk, not a reward. Calling me by my first name, Paul, or by my nickname, Polo, is completely fine by me. Beyond that, no: no face, no full name, no portrait, no studio. Apart from my brands — Openline and cupof.news — nothing about me in particular. And for the same reason, what I’m giving you here is not to be presented as a consulting offer for small businesses or creators: that’s neither my market nor my line of business. It’s a hand given to Tev and the world around him — Odyssée, the esport, the food, the merch — and to nobody else. Sorry to be so firm on this: it’s the one point where I can’t be flexible.
units.NB 3 — cupof.news arrive en octobre. Je: NB 3 — cupof.news lands in October. I’m polishing it right now. The idea is nothing revolutionary, and that’s deliberate: a simple, effective news app, ten stories a morning, no algorithmic feed. The model is freemium — free for the essentials, and genuinely cheap for the personalized selection. Useful for everyone, including an audience that follows Japan from a distance.
units.Tout ça se règle très bien par e-mail —: All of this works perfectly well over email — or over messaging, WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Discord, whatever you already use — and it can stay that way as long as you like; I have nothing to impose on you. It’s just that if the collaboration takes shape and becomes at all regular, I like to put faces to the conversation, and fairly early. A relaxed day with Tev and whoever you want, rather than a thirty-minute call.
units.New York ou Lisbonne, comme vous préfére: New York or Lisbon, whichever you prefer and whenever your dates allow — I go back and forth between the two all year: roughly a third of the time in New York, two thirds in Lisbon. Tell me what suits you; fitting around you costs me nothing.
units.À Lisbonne, mon logement est plus grand: In Lisbon my place is bigger than in New York, so I can host two or three of you without any trouble. And show you two or three spots you missed in your video with Massa. No hard feelings, but still.
units.Et si c'est plus simple pour vous, je vi: And if it’s easier for you, I’ll come to Japan, gladly: in that case I only bill the travel, at cost, no markup. You host me there, at the village, in a quiet room, and we settle the rest the usual way — Ubers or the local equivalent, and meals. Nothing else to plan.
Count on 72 hours to five days maximum. No less, because two nights — 72 hours end to end — is the useful minimum: enough to absorb the jet lag and get real full days, rather than a half-asleep round trip. I’ve done Lisbon–New York trips for 24 or 48 hours on the ground, and I remember them badly — nobody decides anything good in that state. And no more, because I can’t free up more than that — it’s a calendar constraint, not a motivation one.
units.Rien de tout ça n'est un préalable. Un e: None of this is a prerequisite. One email is enough to start, even if it’s to say “we’ll take the template, thanks, and leave it there”. That works perfectly for me; that was the whole point.
units.Personne n'est parfait. C'est écrit sur: Nobody is perfect. It’s been written on your clothes since 2021, and that’s exactly why this work was easy to start.
